rows.location: course/modules/S/S7/L05.html Proposition 7.8 and proof (lines 600-607)
rows.evidence: unchanged since 0922fe8 (git diff checked); round-13 evidence: no round-9 change was recorded for this row (it carried the round-8 evidence below). round-8 evidence: Re-derived after the rename A -> D. If the original procedure makes no false rejection, the augmented procedure rejects R = R0 + D' with D' = min(D, m - R0) <= D, at most D' of them false; R = 0 gives FDP = 0; otherwise FDP <= D'/(R0 + D') <= D/(R0 + D) because x -> x/(R0 + x) is increasing; and D <= gamma R0/(1 - gamma) iff D (1 - gamma) <= gamma R0 iff D <= gamma (R0 + D), so FDP <= gamma. Hence {FDP > gamma} needs a false rejection by the original procedure: probability <= alpha. Correct, and the letters D, D' no longer clash with the active set A.

rows.evidence: unchanged since 0922fe8 (git diff checked); round-13 evidence: Re-derived at 45559ab (the passage around (c) changed). For d_t = phi d_{t-1} + e_t with iid e of variance s^2: the marginal variance is s^2/(1-phi^2); the long-run variance (sum of autocovariances, gamma_h = phi^|h| s^2/(1-phi^2)) is s^2/(1-phi)^2, so T Var(dbar) -> s^2/(1-phi)^2. The iid-studentized t = dbar/(sd/sqrt(T)) therefore has limiting variance [s^2/(1-phi)^2] / [s^2/(1-phi^2)] = (1+phi)/(1-phi) = 1.857 at phi = 0.3 (sd 1.363), as E2(a) and the line-878 bullet say. A single-date bootstrap resamples as if iid, so t* is approximately N(0,1) and its 95% quantile is about 1.645; the test rejects when t > 1.645, with probability P(N(0, 1.857) > 1.645) = 0.1137 (E2(b)). Longer blocks restore the serial dependence in t*, so t* inherits the variance 1.857 and the critical value rises: 0.113 / 0.063 / 0.067 in the snippet (exact rerun), 0.11 / 0.05 / 0.09 in my independent loop version (L05-num-E2). The bullet's claim that the stationary bootstrap 'reproduces the same distortion in t*' is the same fact; nothing in it changed.

rows.evidence: unchanged since 0922fe8 (git diff checked); round-13 evidence: Re-derived. Proposal: J_b = the min(k-1,|R_{j-1}|) strategies of R_{j-1} with the largest t*_{b,i}; e_j = the ceil((1-alpha)B)-th smallest over draws of max^{(k)} over A_j union J_b. Bound: fix a draw and an admissible I subset of R_{j-1} with |I| <= k-1; let x be the k-th largest over A_j union I; at least k statistics are >= x, n_A in A_j and n_I in I; J_b contains at least n_I of R_{j-1}'s statistics >= x (because |J_b| >= |I| and J_b are the largest), so A_j union J_b has at least k statistics >= x and its k-th largest >= x draw by draw; hence c(A_j union I) <= e_j and d_j <= e_j (quantile monotone). Control: the pathwise chain of Theorem 7.10 uses e_{j'} >= d_{j'} >= c(I_0). The sentence changed in 'Comparison' only: 'it rejects at least as much as the generic one and is justified only asymptotically'. Numerical spot check of the bound is not needed for an inequality proved above; the derivation holds.

rows.location: course/modules/S/S7/L06.html lines 269-272 (Proposition 4.3, grade T)
rows.evidence: Statement: with p = 2(1−Phi(z)), z > 0: −e p ln p ≥ e^{−z²/2} for 0 < p ≤ 1/e; the inequality can fail above 1/e (p = 0.6: 0.833 < 0.872). Checks (out_num_prop43.txt): 400,000-point grid on (0, 1/e]: 0 violations, minimum margin 3.1e-5; the crossover p* = 0.580409 (z* = 0.552788) lies above 1/e, consistent with the statement (the page states the sufficient domain only). Notation: Phi and Q are used as in the registry (Phi). PASS.

rows.location: course/modules/S/S7/L06.html lines 274-277 (proof of Proposition 4.3)
rows.evidence: Re-derived step by step. (1) Lemma 2.2's lower Mills bound x phi(x)/(1+x^2) ≤ Q(x) gives phi(z) ≤ Q(z)(z+1/z); with e^{−z²/2} = sqrt(2 pi) phi(z) and p = 2Q(z): e^{−z²/2} ≤ sqrt(pi/2) p (z+1/z). (2) It suffices that −e p ln p ≥ sqrt(pi/2) p (z+1/z), i.e. u(z) = −ln p − c(z+1/z) ≥ 0 with c = sqrt(pi/2)/e. (3) u'(z) = phi/Q − c(1−1/z²) (d/dz of −ln p = phi/Q); phi/Q ≥ z (upper Mills bound, 0 violations on the grid) and z > c(1−1/z²) for z > 0 (c < 1), so u' > 0 (grid minimum 1.52). (4) At p = 1/e: z* = 0.900453 and u(z*) = 1 − c(z*+1/z*) = 0.072789 > 0. (5) p ≤ 1/e means z ≥ z*, so u(z) ≥ u(z*) > 0. (6) The MBF minimality (Theorem 4.2) gives the last sentence. All steps re-derived and the numbers checked in out_num_prop43.txt. PASS.
